headline: Nusrat murder case: HC confirms 2 death sentences, acquits 10
summary: The High Court has upheld the death penalty for two convicts, while commuting four others' sentences to life imprisonment and acquitting 10 people.
details: The High Court confirmed the death sentences of SM Siraj-Ud-Dowlah, the then principal of Sonagazi Islamia Fazil Madrasa, and his aide Shahadat Hossain Shamim in the murder of student Nusrat Jahan Rafi.
The court also commuted the death sentences of four other convicts to life imprisonment, while 10 others who had previously been sentenced to death by the trial court were acquitted.
In a significant move, the High Court directed the law ministry to curtail the criminal judicial powers of the trial court judge, Mamun Ur Rashid, who had sentenced all 16 accused to death.
The court criticized the trial judge for handing down the death sentences in a "mindless and irresponsible manner" and ordered his attachment to the law ministry.
caption:
Two death sentences upheld, 10 acquitted. The High Court has delivered a major ruling in the Nusrat Jahan Rafi murder case.

The High Court confirmed the death sentences of SM Siraj-Ud-Dowlah, the then principal of Sonagazi Islamia Fazil Madrasa, and his aide Shahadat Hossain Shamim in the murder of student Nusrat Jahan Rafi.

The court also commuted the death sentences of four other convicts to life imprisonment, while 10 others who had previously been sentenced to death by the trial court were acquitted.

In a significant move, the High Court directed the law ministry to curtail the criminal judicial powers of the trial court judge, Mamun Ur Rashid, who had sentenced all 16 accused to death.

The court criticized the trial judge for handing down the death sentences in a "mindless and irresponsible manner" and ordered his attachment to the law ministry.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo

headline: NCP claims BNP government has completely failed in first 180 days
summary: National Citizen Party convener Nahid Islam says the government has failed to control commodity prices, maintain law and order, and ensure energy supplies.
details: National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener and opposition chief whip Nahid Islam has declared that the BNP government has "completely failed" in its first 180 days in office.
Speaking at a press conference in Banglamotor, Nahid Islam highlighted failures in controlling commodity prices, maintaining law and order, and ensuring electricity and energy supplies.
He alleged that essential commodity prices have risen while market syndicates remain active, and blamed poor planning for fuel and gas shortages affecting households and industries.
Nahid claimed the country is facing a 43 percent gas supply shortfall, disrupting factory production and employment, and noted that electricity prices were increased despite pledges not to do so.
On agriculture, he stated that politically backed syndicates have forced farmers to pay extra for fertilizer, while the banking sector remains a concern.
He further accused the government of reversing its position on mega projects and abandoning its reform agenda in favor of "old politics."
The NCP and its allies plan to intensify their movement, including long marches in five to six divisions and a grand rally in Dhaka, if the government fails to address these issues.
caption:
BNP government 'completely failed' in first 180 days, claims NCP.

National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener and opposition chief whip Nahid Islam has declared that the BNP government has "completely failed" in its first 180 days in office.

Speaking at a press conference in Banglamotor, Nahid Islam highlighted failures in controlling commodity prices, maintaining law and order, and ensuring electricity and energy supplies.

He alleged that essential commodity prices have risen while market syndicates remain active, and blamed poor planning for fuel and gas shortages affecting households and industries.

Nahid claimed the country is facing a 43 percent gas supply shortfall, disrupting factory production and employment, and noted that electricity prices were increased despite pledges not to do so.

On agriculture, he stated that politically backed syndicates have forced farmers to pay extra for fertilizer, while the banking sector remains a concern.

He further accused the government of reversing its position on mega projects and abandoning its reform agenda in favor of "old politics."

The NCP and its allies plan to intensify their movement, including long marches in five to six divisions and a grand rally in Dhaka, if the government fails to address these issues.
